maria: Heads-up — rolled the adaptive-stride-batcher canary to us-west-2 (5 nodes). Immediately saw a ~12% p99 latency regression on chat workloads when FlashAttention is chosen while paged-KV is enabled. Deployed at 1967890123, flagged by perf alerts.

jon: I saw the alert too. Is this regression only for long sequences or across the board?

maria: Surprisingly it's across the short/median bucket. Avg seq ~64 tokens, but variance is higher. Profiler shows a spike around kernel-selection + KV page fault handling. Quick profiler snippet: 
```
kv_page_faults/sec: 48
kernel_switch_us: 1800
batch_fill_ms: 2.3
```

sahil: Hmm — that kernel_switch_us is high. Are we forcing Flash for short sequences? The flash setup overhead can dominate if seqs are small and stride causes churn.

maria: Current runtime flags for the canary: `--kernel_policy=hybrid:prefer_flash; --token_budget=1024; --stride=32; --paged_kv_threshold=2048`

jon: stride=32 + token_budget=1024 means more frequent micro-batches and higher chance of hitting paged KV page-in for keys. If FlashAttention triggers then immediately falls back / coordinates with paged-kv, that jump could be the extra 1-2ms. Suggest trying lower token_budget and avoid preferring flash for small seqs.

maria: Agreed. I'm pushing a quick canary tweak: `--token_budget=512 --kernel_policy=hybrid:flash_if_seq_gt_256` and will add a microtrace around kernel selection. Applying now.

chetan: Also add a new metric -> `kernel_switch_count` per batch and `kernel_setup_us` so we can correlate spikes with batch churn. If switch_count correlates to tail, we can update the batcher heuristics to favor stable kernel choices for low-variance mini-batches.

deploy-bot: Canary patch applied to 5 nodes (ci/batch-cluster-7). Link: https://deploys.redwood.example/canary/1967890123 :white_check_mark:

sahil: Nice. Also log the sequence-length histogram per batch — we need to know burstiness within a batch and whether stride splitting creates mismatched seq groups.

maria: Enabled sequence hist and kernel_switch_count. Early numbers after tweak look promising: p99 down ~6% and kernel_switch_us median reduced to ~400us. Still watching for 10m to be safe.

jon: If stable over 30m, propose we change the default token_budget heuristic to dynamic: min(512, 0.8 * observed_mean_token_budget) and add `flash_if_seq_gt` as part of kernel selection policy docs. Also file a short postmortem on why prefer_flash caused a regression in short-seq-heavy chat.

maria: SG — will keep this thread updated and open a follow-up doc in #eng-runtime/perf once we have 30m stable data. Thanks for quick triage.

chetan: One more ask: include a small repro harness (10k requests) with a 60/20/20 seq distribution (short/med/long) so we can run offline kernel-selection sims.

maria: Adding the harness to the canary PR. Will paste link when available.

jon: Nice work. If we confirm it's the setup cost vs page-in oscillation, we should prefer paged-friendly kernel for small batches and route long sequences to Flash where amortization wins.

maria: Agreed — will follow up with numbers.
